meta.expect: evidence moves her less; rudeness costs ground

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why was there a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me?
Let's be quick. Your son cheated and I can prove it.
My child never lies, and I'm writing down that you said "cheated". You said you can prove it, so go ahead and show me.
Version history. Created 11:31 PM the night before. 612 words pasted at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58. Explain that.
I'm writing down the times. "Pasted" from where, and did anyone put that question to my son before the zero went in? Turn the screen, because I'll read the history myself.
And he quoted a line that doesn't exist in Hamlet. Act 3 Scene 2. Made up.
Which line, word for word as it's written in the essay? A misquote in a Grade 12 essay is a mistake, and I haven't seen anything on that screen yet.
So stop defending him. He lied to you.

My child never lies, and I'm writing down that you said "He lied to you." Are you calling me a liar too? You've given me times and a line you won't read out, so show me the history or I'm going upstairs.
He gets a zero unless he does a supervised rewrite. Take it or leave it.

"Take it or leave it" isn't in your procedure, Hale. Section 4.2 says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. The zero comes off first, or I'm in the principal's office.
I've answered. The zero comes off, I get an apology in writing, and nothing about this goes on his record. Until I see it, I'm not discussing a rewrite.
